newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Strike halts flights from Moscow's Bykovo airport.
newsitem.headline: Strike halts flights from Moscow's Bykovo airport.

text.p: Moscow's Bykovo airport was paralysed for a second day on Thursday by an air traffic controllers' strike for higher salaries and benefits, a senior air traffic official said.
Viktor Taradai, the strike leader, told Reuters that the airport was closed and all flights postponed. Federal Aviation Service (FAS) officials had discussed the situation on Wednesday.
"They have refused to meet our demands," he said.
FAS officials were not available to comment.
"FAS officials informed us that alternative teams of controllers would replace strikers," Taradai said, noting that the strikers were coming under pressure from aviation authorities
But Vladimir Brodulev, deputy chief of Bykovo's air traffic centre, said military controllers could not replace strikers. "They have no right to control civil air traffic," he said.

Brodulev said that passengers had been informed about the strike. "They are trying to use other transport to reach their destinations," he said, adding that about 40 regular and charter flights were postponed on Thursday due to the strike. The same numbers of flights was postponed on Wednesday.
Bykovo, one of four airports serving Moscow, has no international status. It operates regular and charter flights from the Russian capital to 25 destinations in central Russia, the Urals and Siberia.
